title: Man was created able to obey the law perfectly
source_text: THESIS I. In eo statu homo a Deo conditus est ut posset legi quam Deus ipsi tulit obedientiam integram & perfectam praestare absque omni labe vel culpa. Nec enim aequum fuisset Deum ab innocenti creatura ea exigere ad quae praestanda, vel nullas, vel non sufficientes vires ei concessisset. Atque hoc confirmat scriptura, dum docet [marg.: Eccl. 7. 29.] Deum fecisse hominem rectum. Nec enim posset censeri rectus ille qui sese legi Dei, quae rectitudinis norma est, conformare non posset.
pass_a_gloss: THESIS I. In that state man was made by God that he could render to the law which God gave him an entire & perfect obedience without any stain or fault. For it would not have been fair for God to demand from an innocent creature those things for performing which he had granted him either no powers, or not sufficient ones. And Scripture confirms this, when it teaches [margin: Eccl. 7:29] that God made man upright. For he could not be judged upright who could not conform himself to the law of God, which is the rule of uprightness.
pass_b_english: Thesis I. God created man in a condition in which he could give the law God laid on him a complete and perfect obedience, free of any stain or fault. It would not have been fair for God to require of an innocent creature what he had given it no strength, or not enough strength, to do.
Scripture confirms this when it teaches (margin: Eccl. 7:29) that God made man upright; and no one could count as upright who was unable to conform himself to God's law, the very rule of uprightness.

choices.why: The locus question: whether and how far a person can fulfil the law through Christ's grace.
